title: VILTA: A VLM-in-the-Loop Adversary for Enhancing Driving Policy Robustness

control_signal.value: Scene and environment representation given to a VLM, which edits the future trajectory of a designated risky agent to challenge the ego; designers also set how often challenging scenarios alternate with normal ones.

control_mechanism.value: VLM directly edits a rule-based baseline trajectory (CTRV model fused with map waypoints), followed by B-spline smoothing, sigmoid fusion with the baseline, and an LQR controller for kinematic feasibility.

base_model.value: VLM trajectory editor in the loop with an RL-trained ego driving agent in CARLA; reward combines driving style, following and safety-penalty terms.

datasets.value: CARLA simulator, trained on Town02 and evaluated on Town01, Town02, Town03, with 20 autopilot vehicles per map, one designated risky agent.

metrics.value: Route completion (RC), collision rate (CR), collisions per km (CPM), average speed, total distance, collision speed.

controllability_evidence.value: Edited trajectories have smaller minimum distance to ego and more extreme acceleration and steering than directly generated ones. In challenging scenarios the ego policy gains 13.3% and 25.3% route completion and 28.5% and 39.4% lower crash rate versus VLM-RL and CAT.

stated_limitations.value: Validation is confined to simulation; the rest of the limitations text is cut off in the packet.

notes: Primary goal is robust ego-policy training with a VLM adversary, not a controllable generator; the specific VLM is not named in the packet. Limitations passage truncated.
